mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of UBO's country of residence

Certificate of incorporation of any corporate shareholder or intermediate holding entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Register of directors and shareholders of any corporate shareholder or intermediate holding entity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, directors, and beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Samoa domestic AML/CFT sanctions list, and Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any positive PEP match, sanctions list hit, or adverse media. Screening must be repeated within 48 hours prior to incorporation and annually thereafter pursuant to Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Companies Registry Online Name Search and Reservation Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in the Latin alphabet. Samoan and English names are acceptable. A foreign-language name must be transliterated into roman script and a translation or explanation of its meaning may be required. The name of an International Company must end with 'International', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or an approved abbreviation ('Int'l', 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.'). Punctuation and special characters are generally restricted; names must be easily identifiable and not misleading.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Credit Union, Building Society, Trust, Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Fund, Mutual Fund
Government, Ministry, Authority, Commission, Public Board, Municipality, Central Bank
University, Institute, Chamber of Commerce, Trade Association
Sovereign, National, or Governmental terms implying official patronage
Names implying a connection with the Government of Samoa or a foreign government
Offensive, obscene, or contrary to public interest terms
Terms requiring prior ministerial approval under the International Companies Act, Banking Act, Insurance Act, and Public Finance Management Act
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may (a) modify the proposed name and file a fresh application, or (b) submit a written appeal to the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days of the rejection date, citing the legal basis for eligibility. The appeal will be reviewed within 21 business days. A rejected name may also be re-submitted after a 90-day cooling-off period if the objection is based on likelihood of confusion. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, judicial review is available before the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicature Ordinance 1961.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For Samoa International Companies, a physical registered office in Samoa is mandatory and must be maintained by a licensed registered agent. A virtual office address is not permissible as the statutory registered office. For the data center colocation business, the company may maintain a separate operational site in Samoa or abroad, but the registered office must be a physical Samoan location capable of receiving service of process. Virtual meeting platforms are acceptable for board meetings but cannot replace physical registered office presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of an unannounced physical inspection by the Samoa International Companies Registry or the Central Bank of Samoa is approximately 5% per year during the first year of incorporation. The probability rises to 10-15% if the company is selected for an AML/CFT risk-based examination, if there is a change in registered agent, or if a negative media or sanctions alert triggers enhanced supervision. For a low-risk standard data center colocation business, the baseline risk remains Low_Risk_Standard but does not eliminate compliance monitoring visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 1998 and subsequent AML/CFT amendments; principally Sections 6 (Incorporation), 9 (Memorandum and Articles), 17 (Registered Office and Registered Agent), 25-31 (Directors and Secretary), and 45-50 (Share Capital and Accounts).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation Application together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association and the Consent of Registered Agent (Registrar Form IC-1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a nominal authorized capital (commonly USD 10,000) may be declared at the subscriber's discretion, and no escrow, deposit, or paid-up capital verification account is required for incorporation filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriber, having approved the Memorandum and Articles of Association, adopts and ratifies the registration of the company as an International Company under the International Companies Act 1987. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the initial subscription of ordinary shares set out in the register of members is accepted, and the allotment of such shares to the subscriber is approved. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office and registered agent in Samoa designated in the registered agent's consent are hereby adopted as the company's statutory registered office and registered agent. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the persons named in such consent are appointed as the first director and secretary, to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until removed by written resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa (filing made through a licensed Samoa registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed registered agent to submit a name availability search and Application for Reservation of Company Name to the Registrar. Provide a primary name and two alternate names; avoid names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company and any name implying banking, trust, insurance, or government sponsorship absent a special licence. The application may be filed by email scan or through the agent's portal; upon approval, the name is reserved for three months.
required_dossiers: Application for Reservation of Company Name (Registrar Form)
Proposed company name with two alternate choices
Registered agent engagement letter
Identity verification form of the proposed subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as undesirable or too similar, file a fresh reservation application with substituted names within the same SLA period; a refusal may be appealed by written objection to the Registrar within 21 days, with ultimate recourse to judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents and Registered Agent Consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent under the International Companies Act 1987; Registrar of International Companies, MCIL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English and the prescribed Statement of Particulars, including the Consent to Act as Registered Agent. The subscriber, first director, and secretary execute the documents; signatures are witnessed by the registered agent under AML/CFT client due diligence, including verification checks on beneficial owners. Notarization is not a statutory requirement for Samoa International Company incorporation, but certified identity copies are required by the agent.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (executed)
Consent of Registered Agent (statement of particulars)
Register of Directors and Officers
Register of Members and Shareholders
AML/KYC pack: certified passport copy, proof of residential address, and corporate extract if the subscriber is a legal entity
Beneficial ownership register and declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registrar queries on incomplete execution or inconsistent particulars are cured by filing an amending statement through the agent; minor clerical defects may be remedied by a Notice of Correction filed with the Registrar within 14 days of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of State Filing Fee and Submission of Incorporation Pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, MCIL (over-the-counter and via licensed agent electronic submission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent e-files the executed incorporation pack together with the Registrar Form IC-1 and the payment voucher. The official state filing fee of USD 200 (or equivalent Samoan Tala at the Central Bank exchange rate) is remitted by SWIFT transfer or direct deposit into the Government of Samoa consolidated revenue account; the bank receipt must accompany the filing. The Registrar assigns the company file number upon docketing.
required_dossiers: Registrar Form IC-1 (application for certificate of incorporation)
Execution copy of Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statement of Particulars and Consent of Registered Agent
Official government filing fee payment receipt (USD 200)
Registered agent cover letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the package for formal defects, the agent must rectify and re-file within 10 business days; a re-filing fee of USD 50 may apply. Erroneous refusal or non-registration may be challenged by way of judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Preparation of Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the unique company number and the date of incorporation. The registered agent collects the certificate, prepares the company's statutory register book (members, directors and officers, charges, and beneficial owners), issues share certificates to the subscriber, and records the registered office and registered agent particulars as effective from the certificate date.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (official extract)
Company statutory register book
Share certificates and allotment record
Registered office and registered agent confirmation letter
Company seal (optional, if adopted by the board)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical or identity error, the agent files a statutory declaration and an application for re-issue with the Registrar, paying the prescribed amendment fee of approximately USD 60; corrected certificates are issued within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Written Resolutions and Post-Incorporation Governance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; Companies Registry, MCIL for post-incorporation change filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution adopting the pro-forma First Board Resolution: ratifying share subscription, adopting the registered office and agent, and confirming the appointment of the first director and secretary. The board also approves the opening of bank accounts, adoption of the corporate seal, and engagement of the data center operations service provider. Any subsequent change of directors, secretary, or registered agent must be filed with the Registrar within 30 days of the change.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting or signed written resolution
Share allotment and certificate register entries
Bank mandate and account opening forms
Service provider agreement for data center colocation operations
Change of directors and officers filing (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to file changes of director, secretary, or registered agent attracts a late filing penalty per month of default; cure by immediate submission of the prescribed Form IC-4 with the applicable penalty, or apply for reinstatement if the company is struck off for non-filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa Business Licence Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) for building and land-use permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence (General - Data Processing, Hosting and Data Centre Operation) under the Business Licences Act 1998

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Environmental Registration / Preliminary Assessment; a new-build data center or substantial fit-out involving excavation, drainage, or generator installation may trigger Category 1 Full Environmental Impact Assessment under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004 and its EIA Regulations 2016.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Samoa National Environmental Standards: cooling-tower blowdown and sanitary wastewater effluent BOD not exceeding 25 mg/L and COD not exceeding 60 mg/L; diesel generator exhaust opacity not exceeding 20% on the Ringelmann scale; boundary noise not exceeding 55 dBA daytime and 45 dBA nighttime; spent UPS batteries and e-waste classified as hazardous and removed only by a licensed waste contractor with a documented manifest trail.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) following inspection of fire suppression systems, alarms, emergency lighting, and evacuation routes; Building Occupancy Permit from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI) verifying structural load ratings for raised floors and rack densities; and Occupational Safety and Health workplace clearance covering electrical safety, confined space entry, and emergency power generator areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue (MOR) of the Independent State of Samoa; integrated e-services portal: Matai Online – https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 2020 must engage its licensed registered agent to file Form TIN-02 (Application for Taxpayer Identification Number) with the Ministry of Revenue, attaching the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office address, and passport copies plus proof of identity for all directors and ultimate beneficial owners; MOR issues the TIN within approximately 3–5 business days upon verification. Where the IC derives all gross income offshore, no Samoan income tax registration is required, but a TIN is mandatory as a precondition for GST registration if the IC makes taxable supplies exceeding WST 100,000 in Samoa or elects voluntary GST registration under the Goods and Services Tax Act 2005.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Samoan domestic law. Relevant statutory elections: (1) voluntary GST registration under section 8(3) of the GST Act 2005 for suppliers below the WST 100,000 threshold; (2) written election by the IC to maintain non-resident tax status by keeping central management and control outside Samoa, thereby retaining full exemption from Samoa income tax on offshore income; (3) application to MOR for a binding tax ruling or certificate of exemption under the Tax Administration Act 2015 confirming tax-neutral zero-rating treatment; and (4) under the Limited Liability Companies Act 2018, members may elect member-level pass-through taxation, though such election is not available to the International Company form itself.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST / GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 2005, administered by the Ministry of Revenue of Samoa
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (Samoan Tala) in annual taxable turnover; imported services supplied by a non-resident to a GST-registered Samoan recipient are additionally subject to reverse-charge accounting at the 15% rate regardless of the recipient's turnover threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not applicable: Samoa does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoice API integration, digital stamping, or government clearance portals. Suppliers must issue compliant tax invoices, retain underlying source documents for seven years, and file GST returns electronically via the MOR Matai online portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under section 12(1) of the GST Act 2005 to (a) goods physically exported from Samoa within 28 days of the supply, and (b) services supplied directly to a non-resident customer, for use and benefit wholly outside Samoa, where the supplier has no fixed establishment in Samoa from which the supply is made. Data-center colocation, bare-metal server hosting, and rack-leasing services sold to offshore tenants qualify as zero-rated exported services when invoiced in foreign currency, supported by an export-service declaration, and substantiated by a service contract showing offshore consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoa Customs export entry) evidencing the physical movement or re-export of data-center equipment and associated hardware

Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export; for pure offshore services, a fully executed colocation service contract plus a service-delivery and usage report issued to the non-resident customer
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by an authorized commercial bank in Samoa confirming receipt and repatriation of the foreign-currency consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry of Revenue audits export zero-rating claims under the Tax Administration Act 2015. Shortfall penalties apply as follows: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, and 150% for evasion with fraudulent intent; unpaid GST is immediately clawed back together with interest at 1% per month. Criminal conviction for GST fraud carries a fine of up to WST 50,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years. In addition, MOR may reassess transfer pricing and adjust below-market colocation lease charges between related parties, triggering additional GST, penalties, and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), acting as Exchange Control Administrator under the Exchange Control Act 1975 (as amended), the Exchange Control Regulations 1980, and supervisor of authorized dealers under the Financial Institutions Act 1996; CBS also operates the national clearing and settlement system and the Samoa Automated Transfer System for domestic WST clearing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is partially convertible: current-account payments (services, interest, operating expenses) are processed by authorized dealers without prior CBS approval, whereas capital-account flows (equity injection, shareholder loans, dividend and profit remittance) require CBS authorization or an authorized-dealer declaration with supporting tax clearance and underlying contract documentation. A Samoa International Company (IC) is treated as non-resident for exchange-control and tax purposes; its data center colocation leasing income from non-resident tenants is offshore business income that may be retained in USD without mandatory conversion. Practical legal constraint: an IC is generally prohibited from carrying on business with Samoan residents under section 8 of the International Companies Act 1987, therefore the colocation assets must be physically located outside Samoa and all lease counterparties must be non-resident. Profit remittance to the foreign shareholder is permissible once the authorized-dealer filing is supported by audited financial statements; the restriction on resident business prevents the IC from using a Samoan domestic WST account as its primary revenue account for onshore leasing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 1980, a resident exporter of goods or services must repatriate foreign currency proceeds to Samoa within 3 months from the date of receipt or shipment and must surrender 100% of such proceeds to an authorized dealer in exchange for WST unless the CBS has approved a Foreign Currency Retention Account (FCRA); retention accounts are subject to CBS policy caps and quarterly reconciliation. For the non-resident IC, the statutory surrender obligation does not attach to offshore receipts; however, if any export-proceeds credit is remitted onshore to a Samoan bank, the collecting authorized dealer will apply the 3-month surrender framework by default and convert surplus foreign currency into WST absent a prior CBS retention approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Limited (BSP Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Non-resident International Company USD Multi-Currency Operating Account / Capital Escrow Account (USD and WST sub-ledgers)
International Company USD/WST Transaction Account with Escrow designation
International Company Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account (WST/USD)
Corporate Current Account (WST standard, USD subject to CBS approval)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Samoa does not recognize offshore Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licenses, and the Financial Institutions Act 1996 requires any money transmission or deposit-taking within or into Samoa to be conducted by a licensed bank or licensed money remitter; international EMIs (e.g., Revolut, Airwallex, Wise) cannot clear WST and cannot file CBS exchange-control reports. The IC may use a reputable offshore EMI as a supplementary USD collection account only if the EMI accepts Samoan IC constitutive documents, while the primary corporate clearing account and all SWIFT MT103 settlements to and from Samoa must remain with a licensed Samoan authorized dealer, typically BSP Samoa.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory regime permits fully remote onboarding for a non-resident IC at tier-1 Samoan banks. In practice, at least one director or the appointed authorized signatory must physically attend the Apia branch, or alternatively a licensed Samoan registered agent (lawyer, accountant, or other AML/CFT reporting entity) must physically verify the identity of all directors and beneficial owners, witness signatures, and issue a formal introducer letter; the bank then conducts a video KYC interview with the UBO as a supplementary control. Accounts will be declined without a physical visit or a certified professional introducer with sampled attestation documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: nominee director or trust structure obscuring the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Certified register of beneficial owners maintained under the International Companies Act 1987; 2) Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); 3) corporate structure chart identifying every natural-person UBO with more than 10% interest; 4) notarized or apostilled passport copies of each UBO; 5) signed statutory declaration from the Samoan registered agent confirming identity verification and the source of the client relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: source of funds for inbound equity capital injection funding data center leases and prepaid bandwidth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Audited financial statements or management accounts of the parent or shareholder for the last two years; 2) executed colocation lease agreement and a rolling 12-month invoice forecast; 3) shareholder resolution authorizing the capital injection; 4) six months of bank statements from the remitting account at the originating overseas institution; 5) tax certificate of residence or tax clearance certificate of the shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: sanctions or adverse-media screening of data center tenants with virtual-asset or high-risk business profiles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Completed AML counterparty questionnaire covering each tenant; 2) sanctions-list screening results against UN, OFAC, EU, and UK lists for every tenant and its UBO(s); 3) PEP and UBO declaration executed by each tenant; 4) contractual warranty prohibiting unlawful use of colocated infrastructure; 5) adverse media search results and independent negative-news analysis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: technology services characterized as intellectual-property rental or digital-asset services triggering enhanced cross-border payment scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Detailed service description confined to ISIC 6209 rack-space and bare-metal hosting with no software licensing; 2) arm's-length pricing methodology with comparable colocation rates; 3) evidence that physical infrastructure is located outside Samoa; 4) customer invoices and hosting statements classified as colocation services; 5) written legal opinion or classification memo from Samoan counsel confirming no resident-business nexus.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity or shareholder-loan capital must be remitted to the IC's USD account at the authorized dealer (e.g., BSP Samoa) via SWIFT MT103 using a recognized purpose code (e.g., G110 Equity Capital or Corporate Credit Capital Contribution); the remitter must supply a certificate of source of funds, and the authorized dealer files the inward-remittance declaration with the CBS. As the IC is non-resident, the USD balance may remain unconverted, but any conversion to WST or onshore application above the de minimis threshold requires CBS approval through the authorized dealer. All remittances must match the IC's SIFA-registered legal name to avoid rejection; pre-notification by SWIFT MT199 or tested telex to the receiving bank is recommended for amounts exceeding USD 1,000,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational trade settlements for server procurement, rack hardware, bandwidth, and offshore data center rent are executed via SWIFT MT103 corporate wires from the Samoan USD operating account; capital-intensive equipment purchases may be confirmed through an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit issued by the Samoan bank via MT700 with the seller's bank as beneficiary. Monthly tenant collections may be aggregated through US ACH by the tenants and then pooled into the Samoan USD account via MT103; all onshore WST disbursements for agent fees, notarization, and FIU compliance run through the national clearing and settlement infrastructure operated by the CBS via the authorized dealer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/WST forward contracts with a licensed Samoan authorized dealer for maturities up to 12 months, supported by underlying trade documentation required by the CBS
Cross-currency swap (USD/WST) with the IC's authorized dealer where the CBS has issued a no-objection letter for the specific notional and tenor
Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) in USD/WST executed with a non-Samoan investment-grade bank, settled offshore in USD without WST delivery and not routed through any Samoan clearing account
Over-the-counter average-rate forward or European-style option contracts with a CBS-approved offshore bank, provided premiums and settlements are booked offshore in USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (International Company Annual Renewal Form)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 10% of the annual fee per month or part of a month; if unpaid for 3 consecutive months, the Registrar may initiate administrative strike-off and dissolve the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government License Fee (included in annual return filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the incorporation anniversary date; grace period ends 30 calendar days after
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest accrues on arrears and the company is removed from the register of international companies; restoration requires a special court application and reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Resident Agent Confirmation (part of annual renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed registered agent and Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the Annual Return by the 30-day post-anniversary deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed registered office and agent in Samoa constitutes a continuing default offence; penalties up to 5 penalty units per day and potential strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a Samoa International Company unless it carries on banking, insurance, trust, or investment business as defined under the International Companies Act, or the Registrar requires an audit by reason of the company's size, ownership, or public interest. For such cases, an independent licensed auditor must be appointed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for entities required to present financial statements; otherwise, general acceptable accounting principles (Local GAAP) may be used for internal records. Financial statements do not need to be filed with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must annually confirm its beneficial ownership information to the registered agent and update the beneficial ownership register. Any share transfer occurring in the preceding year must be recorded before the annual return is submitted. The registered agent is responsible under Samoa's AML/CFT framework to verify UBO changes and retain evidence for 7 years.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 1,200 per annum for a licensed Samoa registered agent and registered office service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable under statutory exemption; if a voluntary review or IFRS audit is commissioned, the typical range is USD 2,500 - 5,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate for domestic companies; Samoa International Companies (ICs) are fully exempt on all income derived from outside Samoa.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate for qualifying ICs under the International Companies Act 2008: no income tax on offshore colocation/revenue, no capital gains tax, no estate or stamp duty, no exchange control. Domestic non-IC companies pay 25%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR-C1 (Company Income Tax Return) via the Samoa Inland Revenue Department e-Services portal (IRD Online Tax System); paper filings accepted at the Ministry of Revenue, Apia.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; tax year runs 1 January to 31 December. Taxable companies also pay quarterly provisional tax; exempt ICs file annually solely to affirm the exemption.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 4 months after the end of the income year (i.e., 30 April for a 31 December year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part A - Box 1a (TIN and Company Registration Number)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Samoa Taxpayer Identification Number plus the International Company registration number issued by the Registrar of International Companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the IC certificate number; non-resident ICs may list the local registered agent as correspondent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calendar tax year (1 January to 31 December) of the reportable colocation/leasing income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offshore ICs report on the calendar year in which lease revenues are received.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income derived from Samoa sources before any deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: IC claiming exemption: enter 0; attach the exemption worksheet, IC certificate, and a brief description of the colocation services. Income sourced outside Samoa is non-assessable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions claimed against assessable income: depreciation, rent, utilities, staff costs, and interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No deductions are claimed where assessable income is nil; maintain records to support any credit position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable gross income minus allowable deductions; nil for a fully exempt IC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Schedules must reconcile to audited accounts where gross turnover exceeds WST 1,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (WST) multiplied by 25% for companies outside the IC exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: enter 0. Non-exempt ICs compute tax on domestic (Samoa-source) income only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits and foreign tax credits applied against the assessed income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs cannot claim imputation credits; foreign tax credits require an attached tax residency certificate (TRC) and DTA relief form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part F - Box 8 (Declaration and net tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund, date, and signature of a director or authorised corporate officer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration certifies no unauthorized Samoa-source trading; false declarations expose the signatory to criminal penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of assessed tax (minimum WST 100); late payment interest accrues at 2% per month (24% p.a.); persistent default triggers the Commissioner's default assessment, a 20% evasion penalty, and rejection of the IC annual license renewal.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Samoa levies no dividend withholding tax on distributions by a Samoa company to resident or non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For interest and royalties qualifying under Samoa's double taxation agreements (Australia and New Zealand), the recipient must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority; (2) submit a Reduced Withholding Rate application (IRD Form W-1) to the Samoa Inland Revenue before the payment date; (3) provide the TRC and completed treaty statement to the Samoan payer; and (4) retain all documents for 7 years. Dividend remittances by an IC require no treaty step because the statutory rate is nil.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory; 10% under the Samoa-Australia and Samoa-New Zealand DTAs. Interest: 15% statutory; 10% under both DTAs. Dividends: 0% statutory. Payments to tax havens with no DTA remain at the 15% statutory rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 5,000,000 aggregate annual related-party cross-border dealings. Samoa has no codified Local File/Master File regime, but the Income Tax Act 2014 and Tax Administration Act 2014 impose contemporaneous arm's-length documentation and a 7-year record retention duty on all related-party international dealings.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: OECD/EU-aligned Economic Substance Rules apply to Samoa International Companies. An IC deriving data-center colocation income must perform core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Samoa: physical Tier-3/4 server premises, locally engaged technical staff, local payroll and rental expenditure, and board meetings held in Samoa. An annual economic substance declaration must be filed with the Registrar of International Companies; failure to substantiate presence results in loss of the IC tax-exempt status and re-assessment at 25%.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Misreporting Domestic Income as Exempt Offshore Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An IC knowingly treats Samoa-source colocation receipts (leases to Samoa residents, local power and network charges billed in Samoa) as offshore income to zero out the 25% corporate tax, using false invoices or backdated contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2014: shortfall penalty of 200% of the tax underpaid; evasion conviction carries a fine not exceeding WST 500,000 and/or imprisonment up to 7 years; default assessments are immediately enforceable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: directors are jointly liable for unpaid tax and penalties; civil recovery orders, travel bans (warrant for non-removal), and imprisonment up to 7 years may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Structure - Zero Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an IC with a non-existent registered office, no data center in Samoa, or a mere post-box while leasing server racks to foreign tenants; failure to file the annual economic substance declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Companies Act 2008: deregistration by the Registrar, WST 100 per day late fee on annual license arrears, and forfeiture of the IC exemption; strike-off can occur without court order after 3 months' continuous default.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Registrar may apply to the Court for a 5- to 7-year director disqualification; travel bans and asset confiscation apply; shareholders face clawback of upstreamed dividends.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Violation - Laundering Colocation Rental Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Channeling lease deposits and monthly ACH/SWIFT rental payments through layers of IC bank accounts to conceal beneficial ownership; failing to file suspicious transaction reports under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007: fine up to WST 1,000,000 for a body corporate; imprisonment up to 14 years for individuals; servers and rental proceeds are subject to confiscation and freezing orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal AML prosecution, exclusion orders, travel bans, mutual legal assistance extradition (including to Australia and New Zealand), and civil liability for restitution of laundered proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Prohibited Domestic Business - Unlawful Samoa-Source Trading
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An IC leases rack space or bare-metal servers to Samoa Government Ministries or Samoa-resident enterprises and receives monthly WST payments, converting the exempt offshore status into unlawful Samoa-source business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Companies Act 2008 and Income Tax Act 2014: automatic forfeiture of the IC exemption; re-assessment of 25% tax on all previously exempt profits within the 7-year limitation period; penalty of 50% of the omitted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for omitted corporate tax and withheld amounts; court-ordered civil restitution from personal assets; immigration stop-lists prevent departure before full settlement.
